text:
anika: quick heads-up — I ran into confusing auth behavior while updating the sample apps. js samples read REDWOOD_KEY, python samples read REDWOOD_API_KEY, and the Go example uses RW_TOKEN. new devs copy these verbatim and hit auth errors. :weary:
tony: ugh. Are SDKs even consistent about which scope (project/org/account) they prefer?
anika: no — different orderings. go: org -> account, python: project -> account -> org, js: account only unless RW_SCOPE is present.
reno: that variability is the root cause. suggests we need a canonical env var scheme and documented precedence.
sophie: proposal: single canonical key env var REDWOOD_API_KEY. separate scope env var REDWOOD_SCOPE that accepts values like "project:<id>" or "org:<id>". SDKs should parse REDWOOD_SCOPE, not invent new names.
tony: agreed. also: how do we support short-lived creds? CI wants auto-rotating tokens stored in secret managers. current SDKs read env on startup and cache forever. leads to unexpected 401s.
anika: we hit that in CI: long job dies mid-run after token TTL. no transparent refresh path.
reno: small design: SDKs accept an optional credential provider function (sync or async) that returns { token, expiry } — SDK calls it on init and again on 401 (once) and transparently retries the failed request. identical semantics across languages.
sophie: yes please. pattern like:
```
// pseudo
client = new RedwoodClient({
  credentialProvider: async () => {
    return { token: await fetchFromSecretManager(), expiresAt: Date.now()+300000 }
  }
})
```
sdk should only auto-retry once to avoid infinite loops if provider misconfigured.
tony: SDKs should also expose a small helper to wrap GCP Secret Manager / AWS Secrets Manager so sample apps can show a working example.
anika: ops wants the fallback behavior too — if env var is present use it first, otherwise call provider. and log at info when provider used.
reno: for backward compat, let's add deprecation warnings: accept old names RW_TOKEN, RW_KEY as fallbacks but log a WARN once per process encouraging REDWOOD_API_KEY. plan to remove fallback in 6 months.
sophie: docs + migration: I'll write a devportal page "Auth envs & rotation" showing precedence, credential provider API, and sed snippets to mass-replace old vars in repos: e.g. `sed -i 's/RW_TOKEN/REDWOOD_API_KEY/g' .env*`.
anika: good. devex task: add a preflight lint in SDK release pipeline that scans sample apps and flags non-canonical env var names. tony can add that as a CLI check.
tony: yep — I'll open a GH issue for the lint rule.
dev-bot: issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex/issues/912 — "canonicalize REDWOOD_API_KEY + credential-provider API + sample helpers" (created by dev-bot)
reno: I'll open the provider API RFC and a small python PR to add provider arg + single-retry-on-401. We'll include unit tests that simulate expiry mid-request.
anika: I'll update the sample apps and README to use REDWOOD_API_KEY and reference the new doc. tagging @devex for review.
sophie: timeline proposal: doc + lint + sample app fixes in 2 weeks; SDK provider implementation + cross-language parity in 4 weeks; deprecation warning window 6 months.
anika: sounds good. assigning tasks and will follow up with PR links in this thread. thanks all! :rocket:
